title: Active-driver mounting holes bridge the gasket and vent the sealed chamber
evidence: Cabinet driver bore radius 44.350 mm; driver gasket annulus radius 45.850 to 51.900 mm (driver_gasket = bore + 3.0 -> seat).
Dayton ND91-4 bolt circle 93.3 mm with four 4.0 mm holes gives a hole footprint at radius 44.650 to 48.650 mm (config/components.yaml).
The hole inner edge (44.650) lies 1.200 mm INBOARD of the gasket inner edge (45.850), so no continuous inboard sealing land exists.
The active-driver clamp ring inner bore radius is 48.000 mm (driver_outer_diameter - 7.2), leaving 3.350 mm of radial hole width exposed to atmosphere inside the ring bore.
Complete path: chamber -> bore (r<44.350) -> gap under the driver flange (r 44.350-45.850) -> mounting hole (r 44.650-48.650) -> open inside ring bore (r<48.000). Four such holes.
Control case: the passive radiator is correct. Gasket radius 52.600-61.300, hole footprint 53.600-57.900, giving a continuous 1.000 mm inboard land.
No guide instructs the builder to plug or seal the driver mounting holes; grep of docs/*.md finds no such step.
exports/gasket_templates/driver_gasket.dxf cuts this same annulus, so the builder cuts the leaking gasket.
engineering_consequence: The enclosure is not sealed. Roughly 50 mm2 of unintended vent area bypasses the driver gasket, which invalidates the passive-radiator alignment, the modelled 60.0 Hz Fb, the 56.9 Hz f3, and every derived output figure. The leak-test step in assembly would fail, or worse, pass at 100-250 Pa while still ruining the acoustic Q.
verification_method: Compute driver_bore_diameter/2, (driver_bore_diameter+3)/2, driver_seat_diameter/2 from load_design_parameters(); compare with (bolt_circle_mm -/+ mounting_hole_diameter_mm)/2 from selected_components(); compare hole inner radius against (driver_outer_diameter-7.2)/2. Reproduced independently of the reporting agent.
resolution: Fixed. driver_gasket now spans the whole flange underside (inner diameter at the driver cutout, outer at the flange rim) instead of bore+3.0 to seat, so all four unused mounting holes are covered from below and no open gap is left inboard of the gasket. The gasket also no longer overhangs the flange edge, so the whole band is compressed. Note the residual: the ND91-4 leaves only 0.4 mm of flange between its mounting hole and the cutout, so the inboard sealing land is inherently short. Confirm the seal with the 100-250 Pa leak screen and treat a failure as a driver-data problem to re-verify against the physical part. A new sealing gate now models the component flange; verified to FAIL on the previous annulus.

title: Ballast lid bosses are almost entirely unattached to the tray body
evidence: ballast_lid_fastener_positions returns (+/-60.2, +/-66.2); the tray outer extent is 120.0 x 132.0 mm, so half-extents are 60.0 and 66.0. Every boss centre lies outside the tray body, at a rounded corner.

Boolean intersection of one 9.4 mm diameter x 12 mm boss with the bare tray body is 5.81 mm3, i.e. a mean bonded cross-section of 0.484 mm2 over the 12 mm height. A fully embedded boss would give about 69.4 mm2.
Bounding box confirms the overhang: ballast_cartridge and ballast_cartridge_lid are both 129.80 x 141.80 mm rather than 120 x 132 mm.

Root cause: the offset in ballast_lid_fastener_positions is measured from the steel PLATE edge (plate_width/2 + boss_outer_diameter/2 + 0.5) instead of the tray wall, and a 9.4 mm boss cannot fit inside a 4 mm tray wall in any case.
These four bosses carry the heat-set inserts retaining the steel stack; reports/validation/center_of_gravity.json records a 155 N design load.
engineering_consequence: The bosses are expected to shear off during heat-set insert installation or on first tightening. Ballast retention of roughly 1 kg of steel above the user is unverified, and the lid may not be securable at all.
verification_method: Rebuild the bare tray as ballast_cartridge does (rounded_prism(120,132,14,0,10).cut(rounded_prism(112,124,12,2,6))), construct one boss cylinder at a fastener position, and take the boolean intersection volume. Reproduced independently of the reporting agent.
resolution: Fixed. ballast_lid_fastener_positions is now derived from the tray wall (mid-side of each wall face) rather than the steel plate edge. Bonded cross-section per boss measured at 32.359 mm2, up from 0.484 mm2, a 67x improvement, and identical on all four bosses. Screw axes sit 5.0 mm clear of the steel plate footprint.

title: Required official part O06 is absent from the assembly model and every geometry gate
evidence: official_top_plate_snap_in_diffuser_ring is listed in OFFICIAL_PRINT_PARTS_REQUIRED as O06 and ships to builders as PRINT_THESE_FILES/3_SQUIRCLE_TOP_PARTS/06_SNAP_IN_LIGHT_RING.stl.
UPPER_STACK in src/satellite1_ultra/official.py is (MID_PLATE, MID_PLATE_THREADS, TOP_PLATE, PCB_SPACER, LOCK_RING) and does not include it.
release_parts() therefore never contains it, so it appears in no assembly STEP export, no render, and no collision or clearance evaluation.
engineering_consequence: Builders are told to print and install a part whose fit has never been checked against the Ultra shroud, divider, or upper stack. Any interference would only be discovered physically.
verification_method: Compare the names in OFFICIAL_PRINT_PARTS_REQUIRED against UPPER_STACK, and against the keys of release_parts(include_official=True).
resolution: Fixed. TOP_PLATE_SNAP_IN_DIFFUSER_RING added to UPPER_STACK, so O06 is now in release_parts, the assembly STEP exports, the renders, and official_upper_solids. It is therefore covered by the printed-vs-official clearance and collision gates, which pass with it present.

title: BOM B02 tuning mass is unreachable with the hardware it specifies
evidence: reports/acoustics/summary.json gives added_pr_mass_each_g = 0.7818 g, and BOM item B02 specifies M6 stainless flat washers in identical stacks totalling that mass.
One M6 DIN 125A washer (12.0 OD, 6.4 ID, 1.6 thick, 7900 kg/m3) computes to 1.02 g, which already exceeds the whole target by 30%.
The smallest achievable increment with the specified hardware is therefore larger than the specified total.
engineering_consequence: The builder cannot hit the modelled tuning mass using the specified parts. Fitting one washer per radiator over-masses by about 30% and lowers Fb below the model; fitting none leaves the radiators untuned.
verification_method: Compute washer volume pi/4*(12^2-6.4^2)*1.6 = 129.5 mm3 and multiply by 7.9e-3 g/mm3; compare against added_pr_mass_each_g in reports/acoustics/summary.json.
resolution: Fixed. B02 is now a self-adhesive lead-free tuning strip trimmed to the target mass with the two sets matched within 0.02 g, instead of M6 washers whose smallest increment (about 1.0 g) exceeds the whole target. The BOM entry states that limitation explicitly, and the assembly step and build book were updated to match.

title: Instructional renders composited parts by artist order rather than depth
evidence: renders.py added one Poly3DCollection per part. Matplotlib depth-sorts polygons only within a single collection and composites separate collections by artist order, so nearer parts were drawn behind farther ones.
Planar walls also tessellate into a small number of very large triangles, and a painter's-algorithm sort ranks each by one depth value, which is wrong for a triangle spanning most of the model.
Antialiased triangle edges at linewidth 0 left pale seams, which made solid surfaces read as wireframe.
engineering_consequence: Assembly diagrams showed parts in physically impossible stacking order, which is actively misleading in a document whose purpose is to show a builder what goes where.
verification_method: Render a scene containing a small solid fully enclosed by a larger one and count pixels of the inner colour; it must be zero. Confirmed zero both before and after the fix, with the ordering defect visible only in multi-part scenes.
resolution: Fixed. Clamped stacks are now measured on the B-rep: a probe just larger than the clearance hole is intersected with the clamped parts at every fastener position, and the run bearing against the mating face is taken. 8 of 11 joints are measured; F01/F10/F11 stay declared because they are official parts. Two declarations were wrong and are now corrected automatically: F06 3.50 -> 2.00 mm (the lid tongue is absent under its screws, which drops that screw from M3x8 to M3x6) and F03 5.50 -> 4.00 mm (the screws do not pass through the divider gasket).

title: Builder documentation never instructs the builder to cut the gaskets
evidence: G01, G02 and G03 are cut by the builder from EPDM sheet using exports/gasket_templates/*.dxf.
The former BEGINNER_BUILD_GUIDE listed the gaskets only in a pre-assembly checklist, and no guide contained a step to cut them or to print the templates at 100% scale.
The assembly steps assume the gaskets already exist.
engineering_consequence: A first-time builder reaches assembly step 3 with no gaskets and no instruction to produce them, and may improvise a seal, which directly compromises the acoustic boundary.
verification_method: Search the generated guides for a cutting instruction referencing GASKET_TEMPLATES; previously absent from the builder path.
resolution: Added Phase 5 of the Build Book, covering 100% scale printing of the templates, the per-gasket table, and the one-continuous-piece rule.

title: Two competing entry-point documents, and a calibration guide named START_HERE
evidence: The release shipped both START_HERE.pdf and BUILD_SATELLITE1_ULTRA_FOR_BEGINNERS.pdf, each telling the builder it was the place to begin, with largely duplicated content.
The calibration guide was published as START_HERE_CALIBRATION_GUIDE.pdf, a third document whose name competed with the first two.
HARDWARE_AND_MATERIALS_GUIDE.md was the only builder guide with no PDF, so it was absent from the release package.
engineering_consequence: A builder had no single authoritative path and had to reconcile overlapping instructions, which is how steps get skipped.
verification_method: Inspect PDF_GUIDES and the release package listing.
resolution: Replaced both entry points with one SATELLITE1_ULTRA_BUILD_BOOK.pdf covering the whole build in nine phases; renamed the calibration guide to CALIBRATION_GUIDE.pdf; added the missing hardware PDF.

title: make clean did not remove all generated documents
evidence: GENERATED_DOCS in cli.py was a hand-maintained list that omitted BEGINNER_BUILD_GUIDE.md and BUILD_SATELLITE1_ULTRA_FOR_BEGINNERS.pdf.
Those two files therefore survived make clean and could be served from a stale build indefinitely.
engineering_consequence: A renamed or retired guide can persist on disk and be shipped, presenting instructions that no longer match the source.
verification_method: Compare GENERATED_DOCS against USER_GUIDES and PDF_GUIDES.
resolution: GENERATED_DOCS is now derived from USER_GUIDES and PDF_GUIDES, so the drift cannot recur.

title: Export staleness is triggered by any change under src, including documentation-only edits
evidence: EXPORT_SOURCE_PATHS includes the whole of src/satellite1_ultra, so editing renders.py or documentation.py marks every STEP, STL and 3MF export stale.
Observed directly: a renders.py edit made tests/test_mutation.py::test_changed_export_source_is_caught fail with 'stale export' until the full geometry pipeline was rerun.
engineering_consequence: Conservative and fail-safe, so it never ships mismatched CAD, but it forces a full multi-hour geometry regeneration for a documentation typo, which discourages small documentation fixes.
verification_method: Edit a documentation-only module and run validate_documentation().
resolution: Left as is. Narrowing this set trades a real safety property for build speed and should be a deliberate decision.

title: No sealing gate modelled purchased component flanges
evidence: Every sealing check in sealing_report measured continuity of cabinet material only.
CR-001 vented the chamber through a purchased component's own bolt holes while all eleven gates reported PASS.
Independent mutation testing also found the fastener gate detected none of seven injected defects, because it is a hand-entered table rather than a geometry query.
engineering_consequence: A whole class of sealing defect originating at the component interface was invisible to the validation suite.
verification_method: Added _flange_hole_seal_checks, which compares each component mounting-hole footprint against the gasket annulus from the shared component_gasket_annulus definition. Proven by restoring the pre-fix annulus in memory: the gate reports FAIL, and PASS once restored.
resolution: Gate added and mutation-tested. The fastener schedule remains a hand-entered table and is still tracked as CR-005.
